text:
marta: quick heads-up — bringing up model `redwood-qlm-v2-q4_0` on the tool-calling eval harness. baseline (float32) had ~96% schema pass; quantized run is down to ~78% with a mix of parse errors and missing fields. logs below.
nolan: do we have a repro prompt that triggers the failure consistently? or is it random across examples?
marta: reproducer attached in thread. example prompt that fails: `Please return a purchase object as JSON { \"id\":..., \"items\": [...], \"total\": ... }`. failures look like truncated json or `null` values in required fields.
sylvie: paste of one failing response:
```
{"id": "ord_1234", "items": [{"sku": "X-1"}], "to": 42
```
(note wrong key `to` and truncated end)
nolan: that smells like early termination / token cutoff or decoding instability. what's the generation config for the run?
marta: run config: `temperature=0.0, top_p=1.0, max_new_tokens=64, streaming=false, function_calling=enabled, schema_strict=true, retry_policy=client`.
kevin: two quick checks: (1) is the tokenizer/byte-pair map identical between float and quantized builds? (2) any difference in EOS behavior (early EOS emission)?
marta: tokenizer tokens identical. kernel/runtime team reported slight differences in attention numeric ranges after quantization. eos emission rate increased marginally.
sylvie: can we try increasing `max_new_tokens` and set `stop` to "\n\n" or explicit suffix token to nudge the model to finish the JSON blob? also reduce temperature to 0.0 (already zero) and force `function_calling` to produce structured output instead of freeform.
nolan: also worth toggling `schema_rescue=true` flow: when parse fails, we re-prompt with the original schema and a few-shot of the expected JSON. that worked for some models before.
marta: ran `schema_rescue` on a small sample (50 cases). pass rate improved from 78% -> 89%, but long tail still fails with truncated tokens.
ci-bot: CI note — rerun job #17821-ml-toolcall-quant with `max_new_tokens=128` started by @marta
marta: results from that rerun: pass->92% on same sample. but latency up ~1.4x; token cost up ~1.3x. still seeing a few malformed keys (e.g., `\"total\"` as string vs number) — implies tokenization/format preference shift.
kevin: if the model tends to wrap numbers in quotes, we can add a post-processor: validate types via JSON schema and coerce where safe (string->number), but be careful for semantic errors.
nolan: alternative: move to function calling where the model returns `name` and `arguments` per the OpenAI-style protocol. the runtime will parse `arguments` as strict JSON — that reduces parser ambiguity vs freeform JSON.
marta: tried `function_calling: force` for 200 cases. schema pass -> 95% and specific type issues dropped. but a few responses had `arguments` with extra trailing comma which still trips strict JSON parsers.
sylvie: trailing commas usually come from generation of `,\n}` when the model hallucinated an extra comma. we should add a sanitize step: (1) quick regex remove trailing commas before `}` or `]` (2) attempt `json.loads` and if fails, run small-rescue prompt: `Please output valid JSON only, no commentary` with the previous output as context.
marta: added sanitize regex + rescue prompt. end-to-end pass for quantized model now ~97% on the internal benchset. still want to understand why quant caused more type/shaping issues.
kevin: can we capture log of logits around EOS for failed cases? if quantization causes EOS token prob spike early, we might adjust decoding penalty for EOS token (increase EOS penalty) as a mitigation.
marta: good idea. filed infra ticket `INF-ml-quant-eos-spike` and attached logs for 12 failing examples. samples show EOS prob jumps at token 21 for many failures.
nolan: mitigation experiments to try in order:
1) increase `max_new_tokens` and explicit `stop` sequence
2) add `eos_penalty = +2.0` (or whatever param our runtime exposes)
3) enable `schema_rescue` with few-shot
4) prefer `function_calling: force` for production tool-call routes
5) post-process sanitization + type coercion
marta: implemented 1,3,5 in staging. 2 requires runtime flag; opened PR to expose `eos_penalty` (cc @eng-runtime). 4 we want as default for internal tool endpoints.
sylvie: one more note — quant noise seems more pronounced on long arrays (items lists). could be KV-cache precision artifacts. add more test cases with long arrays and high cardinality.
marta: added long-array tests to bench. also bumped samples to include edge cases (empty arrays, `null` items, large numbers). will share detailed matrix tomorrow.
nolan: thanks — summary for product: quantized build is viable with mitigations (schema rescue, function calling, sanitizers). cost win still significant. recommend gated rollout behind canary with automatic downgrade to float model when parse-fail rate > 5%.
eval-bot: EVAL ALERT — quantized-canary-01: pass_rate=96.8%, avg_latency=210ms, parse_errors=0.9% — will promote to small canary cohort unless rollback triggered.
marta: ack. I'll coordinate canary and follow up with runtime for `eos_penalty` support. posting reproducer and sample logs in the ticket. thanks all.
